Original · Unique Research · 2025-11-24

Editorial note: This is a historical report of the November 2025 event. Figures, awards, roles and forecasts are attributed to the original report. The headline's 2,000 attendees and the stated 2,200 registrations are distinct figures. No survey sample size or methodology is supplied. The closing invitation and March 2026 Hangzhou plan are preserved as November 2025 announcements, not a current invitation or confirmation of a later event. Unconfirmed official English company names are romanized.

On 2025-11-21, the Grand Metropark Hotel Beijing was filled with attendees as the 2025 AI Creators Summit and CHINA AI 100 & AI Creators 100 Annual Selection, led by Unique Research and co-organized by Yilun AI, came to a successful close. The event's theme was "Pioneering Intelligence, the Age of the Individual," but it was more than a slogan: it ran through the full day of forums, workshops, late-night sessions, and every encounter in the matchmaking conversations.

The event opened with remarks from Unique Research CEO Wu Wei. He first thanked those at the venue and watching the livestream, then shared a figure: registrations reached a record 2,200. More importantly, he placed the "super individual" at the center of the event. Unique Research itself is made up of a group of super individuals, and AI is giving this organizational form its first chance to become mainstream. To make real connections between individuals happen, the event included matched rapid conversations, prize-draw interactions, and activities powered by generative AI / vibe coding, ensuring that the day's exchanges extended beyond the stage.

Jason (Huan Jiachen), Head of Research at Unique Research, then used "The One-Person Company: This Is the Era of AI Creators" to introduce the organization's latest research on AI creators. More than 35% of respondents spend over RMB 3,000 per month on AI tools, with commonly used products ranging from ChatGPT and Midjourney to Jimeng. The reality behind these figures is that AI is pushing the boundaries of what one person can do to a new scale. Jason also offered an important reminder: the goal of AI is not to replace people, but to free them from repetitive work so that creativity and taste can once again become core competitive strengths. What will truly create differentiation in the future is your aesthetic judgment, storytelling ability, and individuality.

Now let us return once more to the day's main stage: the 2025 AI Creators Summit.

The Creator Ecosystem: Organization, Efficiency, and Productivity in the AI Era

The first trend roundtable raised the question to a higher level: when AI makes "one person = one team" possible, how should organizations and individuals change? The session was moderated by Unique Capital partner Zhao Liang and brought together Zhipu AI Senior Vice President Wu Weijie, Aishi Vice President Sun Weizhe, ShengShu Technology Vice President Wang Chuan, and Su Guoli, representing Sand.ai at the session.

Although the guests came from different paths, they reached the same underlying consensus: in the AI era, a "creator" no longer means only a content creator, but anyone willing to use new tools to reorganize processes and rebuild efficiency. Organizational assessment will also shift from "professional skills" toward "ways of thinking and cognition." The real differentiators will be the ability to define goals, exercise aesthetic judgment, and explore the unknown.

3D and Games: AI-Driven Industrialized Production and the Boundaries of Creativity

The next discussion moved into the more technical worlds of visual creation and interaction. Wang Sheng, a partner at Inno Angel Fund, moderated a conversation with Zhao Lu, China President of Collov AI; Wang Bihao, co-founder of Xinying Suixing; Cao Renyi, Vice President of the Li Bai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory; and Li Yingli, VAST's Chief External Partnerships Representative, on the adoption of AI in 3D and gaming.

The conversation had a productive tension. On one side, 3D generation, spatial intelligence, and game Agent systems are bringing scaled industrial production ever closer. On the other, the industry's demands for imagination, precision, and real-time interaction are pushing models toward the boundaries of human creativity. The guests emphasized that the winning factor will not be who has the larger model, but who can keep going deep in vertical data, scenario understanding, and workflows so that AI genuinely becomes part of the production chain.

Short-Form Drama and Film: New Paradigms and Challenges for AI Storytelling

When the topic returned to storytelling, the tension became even more concentrated: AI can maximize output, but the soul of a story remains human territory. The session was moderated by Li Yong, Chairman of Gu Yuan Cultural and Creative Technology, and featured Zhou Zhipeng of Shuimu Intelligence, Liang Wei of MovieFlow, Zhou Liqiang from Chinese Online's AI animation division, and Tong Chao of MOOTION on the panel.

They described how AI is improving efficiency and reducing costs in script adaptation, topic selection, storyboarding, and editing, making the industrialization of short-form drama a real proposition. At the same time, they frankly noted that short-form drama workflows built around intense emotion, powerful hooks, and strong conversion still require extensive, deeply involved human work. In other words, AI is rewriting how stories are filmed, but what should be filmed and why remain the creator's exclusive domain.

Music and Audio: Efficiency and a Personalized Future for AI Creation

The discussion of music and sound repeatedly brought the tension between "efficiency" and "personalization" to the surface. Fan Zhihui, founder of Music Business China / Entertainment Business China, moderated a conversation with Song Kaifa of VMEG, Cheng Zhaoyu of MiniMax, Guo Rui of Mureka, and Yang Yue of 43AI/43Music on AI dubbing and AI music generation.

The guests recognized that AI has broken down barriers to dubbing, arrangement, and style transfer, making cross-language and cross-emotion audio production scalable. They also stressed that because musical aesthetics are subjective, human taste and perspective must still decide what sounds good. AI can raise the floor and expand the range of styles, but genuine personalization must come from a creator's continued exploration of who they are and what they want to express.

At midday, the 2025 CHINA AI 100 ranking was officially unveiled. By carefully selecting 100 AI-native enterprises, Unique Research showcased the strong momentum of China's AI industry as it globalizes.

Vibe Coding: A New Paradigm for Individual Application Development Empowered by AI

An afternoon Vibe Coding roundtable was perhaps the most exciting session for the "super individuals" in attendance: natural-language programming allows non-developers to build products. The session was moderated by Duan Hongyu, CEO of Unique Academy, and featured Si Hongxing of Wanjing Security, Xu Zongze of MetaGPT, and Li Jinglin of DeerAPI, who shared how they use AI to extend the boundaries of individual capability.

Two terms came up repeatedly: "capacity expansion" and "hidden thresholds." On the one hand, AI Coding enables people in product, operations, design, and other roles to build an MVP quickly. On the other, security, engineering, and the operational chain remain unavoidable challenges for a one-person company. AI can take you from 0 to 90 points quickly, but the final 10 points depend on human judgment about scenarios, risks, and productization.

The Agent Economy: Rejecting "Incompetent Agents" and Crossing the Trust Singularity in Enterprise Deployment

As intelligent Agents became an industry focus, the discussion at the event grew more clear-eyed. Zhu He, CEO of Yidian Tianxia (易点天下)'s Intelick, moderated a conversation with Zhai Xingji of Yuhe Technology, Yang Jinsong of Future Intelligence, Hu Xinran of Yixuan Technology, Zhang Wenhao of Dudao Technology, and Sang Zhuohao of Focus Media on why Agents are so often criticized as being incompetent.

The greatest value of the conversation was its shift from "model capability" toward context and requirements engineering. The guests argued that poor Agent performance today is usually not because the model is insufficiently powerful, but because requirements decomposition, scenario matching, context loading, and quality-control systems have not kept pace. The path to crossing the "trust singularity" is to make tacit expert knowledge explicit and process data into reliable chains of action.

Marketing and Sales: Using AI to Empower Sales and Build IP

If the preceding discussions were about production, this one was about monetization. Virgil of Yidian Tianxia (易点天下) moderated a conversation with Wu Bin of Jirui Technology (极睿科技), Heiqiang of Chaohui AI, Li Shouguo of Beta Data, Wang Zhaoqi of Xiaobangbang, and Chen Lingshan of Vidau Technology on how AI is reshaping marketing efficiency and personal IP.

The consensus was direct: AI multiplies the efficiency of content production, advertising, and lead follow-up, but trust must still be forged through a person's own expression and perspective. AI can provide materials and pipelines, while IP remains the advance sales function for a business. The right sequence for building IP is not "get popular first, then make money," but "solve the business first, then use IP to amplify it."

Consulting and Experts: Leveraging Professional Knowledge with AI

As individuals gain AI leverage, the "expert economy" is also being rewritten. Xue Qian, Content Partner at Unique Research, moderated a conversation with Li Ling of StudyX, Bai Shuang of Fuzhiliu, Zhang Minsong of Century Tianhong, Pang Dawei of ChatExcel, and Zhou Ze'an of Biyou Technology on how professional knowledge can be productized and turned into an asset through AI.

The guests discussed the higher requirements for reliability, explainability, and industry knowledge bases in professional settings while also identifying a new opportunity: AI gives tacit experience its first real chance to be captured as a tradable Agent asset. Experts will no longer have to earn solely by selling hours; they may generate passive income through the reuse of knowledge.

E-Commerce and Global Expansion: AI Strengthens the Global Competitiveness of Individual Entrepreneurs

The e-commerce and global expansion discussion pushed the potential of the "super individual" almost to its limit: with AI, one person can conduct business globally. Unique Capital partner Wang Chaochao moderated a conversation with Wei Lihua of HelloTalk, Wang Qing of Boolean Vector, Shu Junliang of MuleRun, Peng Yunye of QuickCEP, and Liu Rushan of Kuangye Qunxing, who shared firsthand lessons from expanding overseas.

One statement in the discussion was especially powerful: AI reduces every source of friction in going global, including language, content, customer service, and advertising, giving individuals their first opportunity to participate in global competition. Yet the true moat remains an understanding of the business and its users, combined with the ability to act and iterate continuously at speed.

Tools and Platforms: An Ecosystem Empowering Individual Entrepreneurs with AI

The final trend roundtable returned to the tools themselves. Wang Lina, founder of Zhiwai Culture, moderated a conversation with Yu Beichuan of Lessie AI, Ma Liang of Silicon Geek, Wang Yang of Molian Technology, Wang Jinxing of Chuangkit, and Li Yangbing, representing WaveSpeedAI in the conversation. Together, they examined how nontechnical entrepreneurs should choose and use tools, and how they can avoid becoming workers for those tools.

The guests emphasized that the ultimate purpose of AI products is not to make people learn more tools, but to have tools remember people, understand them, and take repetitive work off their hands. Individuals should reserve their energy for the capabilities that cannot be commoditized away: action, aesthetic judgment, insight, and differentiated expression.

The forum reached an emotional high point when the inaugural AI Creators 100 was officially unveiled and its awards were presented on stage. The spotlight turned to 100 pioneers using AI to reshape the boundaries of creativity and business, giving concrete names and faces to the idea that the "super individual" is not merely a concept but a reality already unfolding.

Super-Individual Workshops

Running alongside the summit were seven content-rich super-individual workshops organized by Yilun AI, which explored practical methodologies for applying AI in depth.

Yilun AI founder Yi Yating moderated the first workshop, "The Art of Prompting: Core Technologies and Methodologies for Applying AI Efficiently." Yang Yue of 43AI Technology Group, Zhang Kaiyu, co-founder of 43 College, Shi Haixu, CMO of Ruanjimu Technology, and Yunzhong Jiangshu, founder of LangGPT, examined the essence of prompts in depth. The guests argued that prompts are the bridge for aligning people and machines, as well as a mathematical translation of thought. Although there may never be an ultimate, universally applicable "original prompt," mastering structured expression and remaining humble before the model are essential to preventing prompts from failing and activating a model's deeper capabilities.

The next workshop, "AI-Driven Marketing Growth: How Super Individuals Can Break Through in Marketing," was moderated by Xiaohongshu marketing expert Wang Mengke. Product commercialization consultant Wang Man, also known as Abby; Tencent Ads instructor Xiao Q; and Leapo Tech co-founder Manda, also known as Amanda, discussed the restructuring of the marketing industry. The workshop showed how a small team can use AI to deliver the output of a traditionally much larger team and respond quickly to new traffic opportunities. The guests' "Pyramid Freedom Model" and three-dimensional capability model provided a clear path for super individuals seeking to advance.

The workshop "AIGC Video Creation: A Complete Guide from Concept to Breakout Hit" was moderated by Yilun AI partner Zhang Yuanyuan. Long Yitong, founder of Yuemo Studio; Wen Qin, founder of Wenweisi Studio; Senhai, founder of Senhai Yingguang Studio; director Hebi of Pixel Without Borders; and director Zhou Xiangu of URSA Studio spoke candidly about the "anxiety of choice" in creative work. Faced with the rapid pace of technological change, the guests agreed that AI is a partner rather than a replacement. Creators should double down on curiosity and aesthetic judgment, taking action to establish themselves in a field rather than remaining trapped in anxiety.

In the afternoon, Unique Capital partner Zhao Liang moderated the workshop "AI Motion Comics: From Generation to Storytelling, Unlocking New Possibilities in Comic Creation." Producer Maiyun of Mantan (漫谭), Chai Wen, founder of Yijie Chuangxiang (艺界创想), and Zhou Zhipeng, co-founder of Shuimu Intelligence, described 2025 as "the first year of AI motion comics." Technology has reduced production costs to the range of several thousand yuan and dramatically shortened production cycles. Although a mass-market breakout has yet to arrive, the rise of UGC and the surge of specialized content are already clear trends; the future will be a new creative ecosystem in which people and AI coexist.

The following workshop, "AI Short Drama: Driving a New Era of Industrialized Content Production," was also moderated by Yilun AI partner Zhang Yuanyuan. Chen Kun, founder of AIpai; President Huang, founder of the Shanghai creative agency Aimwise; Zhang Rui, COO of StoReel; Yanchuan, founder and director of CoreX-AI Film Studio; and Huang Luxiang, Vice President of Business at Jinghai Shibei, discussed the current semiautomated state of live-action AI short drama. The guests attributed the absence of breakout hits to the difficulty of scaling output and the lack of variety in formats. They advised practitioners to develop expertise in both filmmaking and AI, actively explore new business models such as international expansion, and find the path that fits them.

Technology content creator Captain AI Leng moderated the workshop "AI-Empowered Independent Media: New Strategies for Content Creation and Audience Growth." Yubo, founder of YouMind; Ren Xin, a partner at Sky9; and Frank, known as AI Yilei, founder of QLab, discussed the future of independent media. The guests noted that an AI Agent can equip an individual with greater capabilities, and that "AI partners" may even emerge in the future. The core strategy is to build strong IP, use AI as leverage, establish deep trust with users, and create a profitable loop from content creation to digital products.

The closing workshop, "Vibe Coding: A New Programming Paradigm Driven by Natural Language," was moderated by AI product creator Uncle Huang. Jiamu, co-founder of LangGPT; Yang Zehao, founder of Symbol Interaction; and Qiao Xiangyang of Liehe Technology, formerly an AI product manager in TT commercialization, again focused on Vibe Coding. They shared firsthand practices, including using natural language to develop APP features and creative plans. This suggests that programming will become a foundational form of general literacy: entry-level engineering roles may decline, but super individuals with distinctive value will enter a golden age.

Late-Night Sessions for Creators

When night truly fell, the Beijing gathering did not disperse. Instead, it continued growing in a more grounded form. The daytime Panel and Workshop sessions had already broken down the trends, methodologies, and toolchains in detail, but in the late-night sessions, the real entrepreneurial drive, pressure of trial and error, and possibilities for collaboration brought to the foreground by AI came surging into view.

The late-night session hosted by the Chuhaiqu Incubator, together with its Beijing offline MeetUp, concluded successfully. Chen Feng, a partner at Chuhaiqu, invited YouMind founder Yubo, QuickCreator co-founder Yan Zhitao, ListenHub founder Juzi, former ByteDance commercialization AI product manager Xiangyang Qiaomu, and Yuhe Technology founder Zhai Xingji to share entrepreneurial lessons and project updates, while also announcing a new global-growth business. The program included rapid project showcases and open networking, creating a relaxed but substantive setting for guests and participants to connect in depth and injecting new inspiration into partnerships and innovation in international expansion.

The AGI Villa X Datawhale late-night session on "Agent Technology and Entrepreneurial Deployment" also concluded successfully. It was initiated by Darren, Datawhale city lead and an AGIVilla partner, and used an open format that encouraged participants to share Agent-related ideas, showcase project outcomes, and discuss technical and product bottlenecks together. The gathering brought innovators, practitioners, and explorers together, using open dialogue to create a platform for ideas to collide and partners to connect, helping Agent technology move steadily from concept to real entrepreneurial deployment.

The Vitally AI Studio event "All About Video," led by VitallyAI founder Alvin, also concluded successfully. Its program covered the latest global AI video trends, video-platform tools, commercial advertising, automated publishing, digital-human operations, AI short-form drama, virtual idols, and other topics, attracting professionals from film and television production, advertising and marketing, AI investment, and technology. Guests included Sun Weizhe, Head of Enterprise Services at Aishi; MovieFlow founder Liang Wei; Gary, a super-individual Agent developer; Zhang Pinpin, founder of Yongbao Zhixu; and super creator "Factory Director Xiong." The tightly structured event featured TED-style talks and open discussion. Vitally also previewed a new one-click product-promotion video product for e-commerce, creating a platform for collaboration across diverse AI video applications and their evolution alongside future technologies.

Preview: 2026 Hangzhou AI Tech Week

The end of the Beijing gathering was therefore not a full stop marked "event successfully concluded," but more like an echoing reminder: in the AI era, what super individuals truly need has never been only stronger tools, but clearer direction, bolder action, and peers who can propel them forward. By day we clarified where the industry is going; by night we held one another's hands more firmly. When we meet again, we hope what you bring is not "I learned something else," but "I used AI to turn something into reality."

And here is one final reveal: in 2026, the Unique Bloom will no longer be just "one day of excitement," but will expand into a full AI technology week. Planning and partnership outreach for #2026 Hangzhou AI Tech Week are already underway. If you want to secure an earlier position in the next wave of the AI industry and help us build a bigger stage, we welcome an early conversation. Our ambition is not merely to extend the duration of the event, but to make the Unique Bloom the most worthwhile AI Tech Week to attend in the Eastern Hemisphere. We look forward to gathering again in Hangzhou in late March 2026 and taking this creative energy even further together.

Historical image notes: The original event photographs also contain the following readable background information. These notes describe the source images, not an independently reconstructed list of every award recipient.

Survey slide (source image 4): The research dashboard includes charts headed respondent identity, industry, age, gender, style, spending and AI tools. The AI-tool word cloud visibly includes GPT/ChatGPT and Jimeng. Most chart labels and percentages are too small or overexposed to transcribe reliably from the published photograph, so no additional values are inferred. The spending result reported in the article above remains the source's readable textual figure.

CHINA AI 100 ceremony (source image 9): The backdrop reads “2025 CHINA AI 100” and “Pioneering Intelligence, the Age of the Individual.” Legible names and logos include HelloTalk, BOOLV, midu, Meitu, EGV, 7.Zion, DeerAPI, initi:AI, VidAU and collov.ai. This is a partial transcription of a photographed backdrop, not the complete 100-company list, and it does not identify the people holding certificates. Other small logos, partly hidden lettering and certificate text cannot be reliably read from this source image.

AI Creators 100 ceremony (source image 16): The backdrop reads “AI CREATORS 100 — Creators of the Year.” Readable names or creator handles include AI Huahua de EASON (AI画画的EASON), AI Huazhonghua (AI画中画), AI Yilei Fulan ke (AI异类弗兰克), Bella Ren, Dave, DynamicWang, H Liuliu (H六六), InitialC&G, Jim HuiHui, KK Bushexian (KK不设限), Nenly, OneBrocade Ayi (OneBrocade阿一), Rico Yousanmao (Rico有三猫), San–Shanyu (San-山雨), Vinli Wei'en (Vinli维恩), WAI–Niting (WAI-你听), Yea Yele (Yea野了), Zho, An Shi (安史), Binghe (冰河), Bugu Gugugu BUGU (布谷咕咕咕BUGU), Cao Yiqing (曹一清), Changqin (长琴), Chen Liufang (陈刘芳), Dai Yu (戴钰), Ding Zhenxuan (丁振轩), Duocan Zong Binghao (多参宗冰皓), Du Kun (杜坤), Fan Jingjing (范晶晶), Guizang (归藏), Guchuan Chris (谷川Chris), He Chouwan (何愁晚), Houzi (猴子), Huang Naiyuan (黄乃元), Hua Ranse (花染色), Huo Taiwen (霍太稳), Jiao Bo (焦波), Jichuan (吉川), Lawei Huashou (辣味花手), Luoshihu (骆狮虎), Luo Xiao (罗霄), Liang Feng (梁峰), Nanqiang Rylee (南墙Rylee), Geng Xu (耿旭), Liudehua Jiaoshou (留德华叫兽), Li Mingshun (李明顺), Li Jinglin (李京林), Ruiqi of the VRGC Research Institute (瑞奇，VRGC研究院), Roushu (柔树), Senhai (森海), Shangguan Wenqing (上官文卿), Shanyin (山音), Song Zhixue (宋志学), and Sun Changyue, Xiaolongbao (孙畅悦，小笼包). Handles are romanized where necessary, not presented as verified legal names. Other names are blurred, overexposed or obscured by the people on stage; incomplete characters have not been guessed, and the photograph cannot support a complete 100-person roster.

Unique Capital partner Wang Chaochao moderated a conversation with Wei Lihua of HelloTalk, Wang Qing of Boolean Vector, Shu Junliang of MuleRun, Peng Yunye of QuickCEP, and Liu Rushan of Kuangye Qunxing, who shared firsthand lessons from expanding overseas.

One statement in the discussion was especially powerful: AI reduces every source of friction in going global, including language, content, customer service, and advertising, giving individuals their first opportunity to participate in global competition. Yet the true moat remains an understanding of the business and its users, combined with the ability to act and iterate continuously at speed.

Tools and Platforms: An Ecosystem Empowering Individual Entrepreneurs with AI

The final trend roundtable returned to the tools themselves. Wang Lina, founder of Zhiwai Culture, moderated a conversation with Yu Beichuan of Lessie AI, Ma Liang of Silicon Geek, Wang Yang of Molian Technology, Wang Jinxing of Chuangkit, and Li Yangbing, representing WaveSpeedAI in the conversation. Together, they examined how nontechnical entrepreneurs should choose and use tools, and how they can avoid becoming workers for those tools.

The guests emphasized that the ultimate purpose of AI products is not to make people learn more tools, but to have tools remember people, understand them, and take repetitive work off their hands. Individuals should reserve their energy for the capabilities that cannot be commoditized away: action, aesthetic judgment, insight, and differentiated expression.

The forum reached an emotional high point when the inaugural AI Creators 100 was officially unveiled and its awards were presented on stage. The spotlight turned to 100 pioneers using AI to reshape the boundaries of creativity and business, giving concrete names and faces to the idea that the "super individual" is not merely a concept but a reality already unfolding.

Super-Individual Workshops

Running alongside the summit were seven content-rich super-individual workshops organized by Yilun AI, which explored practical methodologies for applying AI in depth.

Yilun AI founder Yi Yating moderated the first workshop, "The Art of Prompting: Core Technologies and Methodologies for Applying AI Efficiently." Yang Yue of 43AI Technology Group, Zhang Kaiyu, co-founder of 43 College, Shi Haixu, CMO of Ruanjimu Technology, and Yunzhong Jiangshu, founder of LangGPT, examined the essence of prompts in depth. The guests argued that prompts are the bridge for aligning people and machines, as well as a mathematical translation of thought. Although there may never be an ultimate, universally applicable "original prompt," mastering structured expression and remaining humble before the model are essential to preventing prompts from failing and activating a model's deeper capabilities.

The next workshop, "AI-Driven Marketing Growth: How Super Individuals Can Break Through in Marketing," was moderated by Xiaohongshu marketing expert Wang Mengke. Product commercialization consultant Wang Man, also known as Abby; Tencent Ads instructor Xiao Q; and Leapo Tech co-founder Manda, also known as Amanda, discussed the restructuring of the marketing industry. The workshop showed how a small team can use AI to deliver the output of a traditionally much larger team and respond quickly to new traffic opportunities. The guests' "Pyramid Freedom Model" and three-dimensional capability model provided a clear path for super individuals seeking to advance.

The workshop "AIGC Video Creation: A Complete Guide from Concept to Breakout Hit" was moderated by Yilun AI partner Zhang Yuanyuan. Long Yitong, founder of Yuemo Studio; Wen Qin, founder of Wenweisi Studio; Senhai, founder of Senhai Yingguang Studio; director Hebi of Pixel Without Borders; and director Zhou Xiangu of URSA Studio spoke candidly about the "anxiety of choice" in creative work. Faced with the rapid pace of technological change, the guests agreed that AI is a partner rather than a replacement. Creators should double down on curiosity and aesthetic judgment, taking action to establish themselves in a field rather than remaining trapped in anxiety.

In the afternoon, Unique Capital partner Zhao Liang moderated the workshop "AI Motion Comics: From Generation to Storytelling, Unlocking New Possibilities in Comic Creation." Producer Maiyun of Mantan (漫谭), Chai Wen, founder of Yijie Chuangxiang (艺界创想), and Zhou Zhipeng, co-founder of Shuimu Intelligence, described 2025 as "the first year of AI motion comics." Technology has reduced production costs to the range of several thousand yuan and dramatically shortened production cycles. Although a mass-market breakout has yet to arrive, the rise of UGC and the surge of specialized content are already clear trends; the future will be a new creative ecosystem in which people and AI coexist.

The following workshop, "AI Short Drama: Driving a New Era of Industrialized Content Production," was also moderated by Yilun AI partner Zhang Yuanyuan. Chen Kun, founder of AIpai; President Huang, founder of the Shanghai creative agency Aimwise; Zhang Rui, COO of StoReel; Yanchuan, founder and director of CoreX-AI Film Studio; and Huang Luxiang, Vice President of Business at Jinghai Shibei, discussed the current semiautomated state of live-action AI short drama. The guests attributed the absence of breakout hits to the difficulty of scaling output and the lack of variety in formats. They advised practitioners to develop expertise in both filmmaking and AI, actively explore new business models such as international expansion, and find the path that fits them.

Technology content creator Captain AI Leng moderated the workshop "AI-Empowered Independent Media: New Strategies for Content Creation and Audience Growth." Yubo, founder of YouMind; Ren Xin, a partner at Sky9; and Frank, known as AI Yilei, founder of QLab, discussed the future of independent media. The guests noted that an AI Agent can equip an individual with greater capabilities, and that "AI partners" may even emerge in the future. The core strategy is to build strong IP, use AI as leverage, establish deep trust with users, and create a profitable loop from content creation to digital products.

The closing workshop, "Vibe Coding: A New Programming Paradigm Driven by Natural Language," was moderated by AI product creator Uncle Huang. Jiamu, co-founder of LangGPT; Yang Zehao, founder of Symbol Interaction; and Qiao Xiangyang of Liehe Technology, formerly an AI product manager in TT commercialization, again focused on Vibe Coding. They shared firsthand practices, including using natural language to develop APP features and creative plans. This suggests that programming will become a foundational form of general literacy: entry-level engineering roles may decline, but super individuals with distinctive value will enter a golden age.

Late-Night Sessions for Creators

When night truly fell, the Beijing gathering did not disperse. Instead, it continued growing in a more grounded form. The daytime Panel and Workshop sessions had already broken down the trends, methodologies, and toolchains in detail, but in the late-night sessions, the real entrepreneurial drive, pressure of trial and error, and possibilities for collaboration brought to the foreground by AI came surging into view.

The late-night session hosted by the Chuhaiqu Incubator, together with its Beijing offline MeetUp, concluded successfully. Chen Feng, a partner at Chuhaiqu, invited YouMind founder Yubo, QuickCreator co-founder Yan Zhitao, ListenHub founder Juzi, former ByteDance commercialization AI product manager Xiangyang Qiaomu, and Yuhe Technology founder Zhai Xingji to share entrepreneurial lessons and project updates, while also announcing a new global-growth business. The program included rapid project showcases and open networking, creating a relaxed but substantive setting for guests and participants to connect in depth and injecting new inspiration into partnerships and innovation in international expansion.

The AGI Villa X Datawhale late-night session on "Agent Technology and Entrepreneurial Deployment" also concluded successfully. It was initiated by Darren, Datawhale city lead and an AGIVilla partner, and used an open format that encouraged participants to share Agent-related ideas, showcase project outcomes, and discuss technical and product bottlenecks together. The gathering brought innovators, practitioners, and explorers together, using open dialogue to create a platform for ideas to collide and partners to connect, helping Agent technology move steadily from concept to real entrepreneurial deployment.

The Vitally AI Studio event "All About Video," led by VitallyAI founder Alvin, also concluded successfully. Its program covered the latest global AI video trends, video-platform tools, commercial advertising, automated publishing, digital-human operations, AI short-form drama, virtual idols, and other topics, attracting professionals from film and television production, advertising and marketing, AI investment, and technology. Guests included Sun Weizhe, Head of Enterprise Services at Aishi; MovieFlow founder Liang Wei; Gary, a super-individual Agent developer; Zhang Pinpin, founder of Yongbao Zhixu; and super creator "Factory Director Xiong." The tightly structured event featured TED-style talks and open discussion. Vitally also previewed a new one-click product-promotion video product for e-commerce, creating a platform for collaboration across diverse AI video applications and their evolution alongside future technologies.

Preview: 2026 Hangzhou AI Tech Week

The end of the Beijing gathering was therefore not a full stop marked "event successfully concluded," but more like an echoing reminder: in the AI era, what super individuals truly need has never been only stronger tools, but clearer direction, bolder action, and peers who can propel them forward. By day we clarified where the industry is going; by night we held one another's hands more firmly. When we meet again, we hope what you bring is not "I learned something else," but "I used AI to turn something into reality."

And here is one final reveal: in 2026, the Unique Bloom will no longer be just "one day of excitement," but will expand into a full AI technology week. Planning and partnership outreach for #2026 Hangzhou AI Tech Week are already underway. If you want to secure an earlier position in the next wave of the AI industry and help us build a bigger stage, we welcome an early conversation. Our ambition is not merely to extend the duration of the event, but to make the Unique Bloom the most worthwhile AI Tech Week to attend in the Eastern Hemisphere. We look forward to gathering again in Hangzhou in late March 2026 and taking this creative energy even further together.
